subject: Inherited red tests of the retained Quartz package, measured with the canonical runner before the first package group.

inheritedState.deviationFromRequirementText: REQ-CLEAN-006 names two inherited red Quartz turnout tests. The fresh measurement finds three red cases: the two turnout cases plus one scheduler load case that is not a turnout case. The fresh measurement governs and the third case is reported.

cases.redSymptom: Should_get_the_job_accepted fails after 30.005 s with TaskCanceledException at Faulted_Specs.cs line 372, which is the await of the JobCompleted handler. Should_have_published_the_job_completed_event then fails in under a millisecond on the already cancelled task.

competingHypotheses.statement: Cross fixture interference through the process wide Quartz SystemTime that QuartzTimeAdjustment replaces per fixture.
The suspect retry is scheduled but the test rewinds the scheduler clock by 60 s before it can fire.
The attempt faults terminally because the reported fault carries no retry delay, so no retry is ever scheduled.
The host is too slow and a longer timeout would make the case pass.

discriminatingObservations.observation: The fixture run in isolation fails identically: 2 failed, 2 passed, same 30 s timeout.

The captured bus log ends 1.2 s after submission with Job Faulted, JobAttemptFaulted, JobFaulted, JobSlotReleased and CancelScheduledMessage. GetJobAttemptStatus never appears and no retry is scheduled, so there is nothing for a clock rewind to delay and nothing a longer timeout could reach.

cases.provenCause: JobConsumerMessageFilter passes a retry delay to NotifyFaulted only when the job retry policy can retry the exception. JobOptions defaults to Retry.None, so the reported fault carries RetryDelay null. JobStateMachine branches on Message.RetryDelay.HasValue and therefore takes the terminal fault branch. SuspectJobRetryCount, which the fixture configures, is evaluated by GetRetryDelay on the JobAttemptSaga and governs the unresponsive instance path only; it never applies to a fault the instance reports.

correction.change: Configure the job retry policy on the job options and drop the status check choreography of the suspect path from the ordered test.
correction.patternSource: The sibling fixture Submitting_a_job_to_turnout_that_faults_with_retry in the same file already uses SetRetry for a retried job and contains no time manipulation. The correction follows that inherited pattern instead of inventing one.
correction.delimitation: The fixture keeps its distinguishing property, an OperationCanceledException raised by the consumer, while the sibling fixture raises IntentionalTestException. No case is duplicated and none is removed.

measurementChain.change: SetRetry added, inherited 60 s advance kept
measurementChain.result: still 2 failed of 4, but with a new mechanism: the retry now starts, and a late status check of the previous attempt sends a second JobAttemptFaulted that drives JobSaga to Faulted; the successful JobAttemptCompleted is then rejected with NotAcceptedStateMachineException and retried until the test times out

measurementChain.change: SetRetry added, status check choreography removed
SetRetry removed again, aligned choreography kept
measurementChain.result: 2 failed of 4, 30 s timeout on the JobCompleted await
measurementChain.conclusion: The retry policy is load bearing and the failure returns for exactly the asserted property, the missing JobCompleted.

recordedProductObservationNotFixedHere.statement: With a retry in flight, a late status check of the previous attempt can send a stale JobAttemptFaulted that moves JobSaga to Faulted. The subsequent JobAttemptCompleted of the successful attempt is then rejected by the state machine and redelivered indefinitely.
recordedProductObservationNotFixedHere.disposition: Recorded only. This is job service runtime semantics and belongs to the follow-up class of REC-012 and REC-030, not to this cleanup. No product file is changed.

cases.redSymptom: OneTimeSetUp fails deterministically with ArgumentException, an item with the same key has already been added, key ...When_processing_a_lot_of_saga_instances+Stop, raised by SagaSpecification while the state machine is configured.

competingHypotheses.statement: The test state machine declares two saga message specifications for the same message type Stop: the schedule and a separate Event<Stop>.
A product regression introduced by the takeover made SagaSpecification intolerant of duplicates.
Test ordering or shared fixture state.

discriminatingObservations.observation: The upstream baseline file src/MassTransit/Sagas/Configuration/SagaSpecification.cs contains the identical ToDictionary over message types, and the upstream twin test declares the same schedule together with the same separate Event<Stop>. The state is inherited from upstream, not introduced by the takeover.
discriminatingObservations.evidence: git show upstream/master:src/MassTransit/Sagas/Configuration/SagaSpecification.cs and the upstream twin test

discriminatingObservations.observation: The failure is a deterministic configuration time exception in OneTimeSetUp and reproduces in isolation, so no ordering or shared state is involved.

The repository's own green scheduling test ScheduleCorrelation_Specs declares the schedule and consumes it through When(Notify.Received) without a second Event of the scheduled message type. That is the idiomatic declaration this fixture deviates from.

cases.provenCause: The state machine declares Schedule(() => StopSchedule, ...) and additionally Event<Stop> Stopped. Both produce a saga message specification for the message type Stop, and SagaSpecification keys its specifications by message type.

correction.change: Consume the scheduled message through When(StopSchedule.Received) and remove the redundant Event<Stop> declaration.
correction.effect: The behaviour is unchanged and the correlation becomes stricter, because the schedule token is validated.

measurementChain.result: The inherited state itself is the probe: with the duplicate declaration present the fixture fails at configuration time with exactly the duplicate key on message type Stop.

resultingState.gateVerdictReason: The canonical category gate stays red because the six inherited Explicit cases are still not in the not-executed inventory. Making them deterministic and required is REC-024 and is not part of this block. No behaviour test fails any more.
resultingState.honestSummary: Three inherited red cases are causally solved. The remaining gap of this category is exactly the six Explicit cases owned by REC-024.
